body:
# Independent audit: arbitrary centroid graphs and the midpoint-tight gap



Sources:

* Section 6 of `candidate fc860651e80d6fd0`;
* `candidate 1b856082117c9e20`;
* the interface to Section 7 of
  `candidate 58dcf29bfb78a573`.

**Result: PASS.** The arbitrary-centroid extension uses no global shear.
All midpoint comparisons, rather than a chosen forest, are needed.
The compact-gap theorem uses the MAXIMUM root deficit exactly as stated,
requires no fixed total mass, and does not imply saturation at a local
minimum. Coherent has separately completed the full independent audit
of the finite labeled-point theorem; its hypotheses and use in this
assembly were checked again here.

## 1. The one-sided arbitrary-centroid extension

Keep the original ambient coordinates. For a through-point cap at
y=(p,g_p), normalize its nonzero continuous normal to a unit vector u.
Writing x=g_z+xi separately in the volume integral of each fiber gives
the exact threshold

    t_z=-a.(z-p)-u.(g_z-g_p).

This is a change of integration variables within each fiber, not a
claimed nonaffine ambient transformation. The retained centroid set
J is the trace on T={(z,g_z)} of the original closed cap. Its weight
is at least alpha because y is an ATOMIC halfspace center in the full
ambient graph space. For a vertical cap the entire fiber is included
or excluded according to the same atomic base trace, so its mass is
at least alpha. Those vertical caps cannot appear late in a sequence
approaching Gamma alpha, because Gamma<1.

For nonvertical caps the finite extended-threshold argument audited
in `historical context (not an accepted premise)` applies unchanged
to the translated full bodies K_z-g_z. It yields, if equality of the
infimum holds:

    w(J)=alpha;
    limiting thresholds are zero on J;
    limiting thresholds off J are bounded positively away from zero.

Every cap-volume convergence is legitimate for finite unit-normal
limits, and infinite thresholds give empty/full limits. In particular
a support tangency can give zero volume but its support threshold is
strictly positive relative to the interior centroid. Whole-fiber
boundary mass in the vertical case was not approximated away.

Let F be the minimal face of conv(T) containing y. A strictly positive
convex representation of y by EVERY graph point in F exists by the
same relative-interior argument as before. Its two coordinate equations
give separately

    sum_z lambda_z(z-p)=0,
    sum_z lambda_z(g_z-g_p)=0.

They therefore give sum lambda_z t_(j,z)=0 for EVERY member of the
normal sequence, however large a_j becomes. Any excluded face point
would contribute an eventually positive term; included terms tend to
zero and all other excluded terms are nonnegative. Thus every face
point belongs to J. The atomic center property and an exposing ambient
halfspace imply w(F)>=alpha. Positivity of the weights, together with
w(J)=alpha, now forces F intersect T=J and w(F)=alpha.

Consequently w(F)>alpha gives strictness of the actual INFIMUM over
all halfspaces. This is stronger than strictness separately for each
fixed cap. A common ordinary equality direction on F is also necessary
if equality holds, although only the face-weight consequence is used
in the assembly. No converse is claimed: exposing F in graph space
can require a continuous coefficient, which need not isolate every
whole physical fiber over the other graph points.

## 2. The exact interface with the finite labeled-point theorem

Assume every distinct same-parity pair p,q has

    g_((p+q)/2)=(g_p+g_q)/2.

Lattice completeness places m=(p+q)/2 in P. Thus the actual geometric
midpoint of the graph points (p,g_p),(q,g_q) is the listed graph point
(m,g_m). The map p -> (p,g_p) is injective, so there are exactly |P|
graph points and exactly k occupied parity LABELS.

The midpoint may have a different label from its two endpoints. This
is expressly permitted by Section 7 of the finite theorem. Its proof
uses closure for same-label witnesses in the Helly argument, and does
not assume midpoint preservation of labels before the face-incidence
bijection has been established. No claim that T lies in an affine
lattice, or that g is globally affine, is required.

That theorem supplies an atomic center of weight threshold M/k in
the FULL graph space. When |P|>k, its exceptional case of exactly k
equally weighted vertices is impossible, and it supplies a center
whose minimal face has weight >M/k. Section 1 of this audit transfers
that one deterministic graph point to raw mixed depth >Gamma M/k.
It is the actual centroid of its listed positive fiber and hence lies
in S. The weak bound follows in the exceptional case as well.

This verifies the first section of the assembly for every ambient
halfspace, not just those whose integer and continuous coefficients
separate or whose continuous normal belongs to a finite list.

## 3. Why all tight root comparisons give the midpoint graph identity

For each listed pair let A=(K_p+K_q)/2. Actual compatibility gives
A subset K_m, and ordinary Brunn--Minkowski gives

    |K_m|^(1/d)>=|A|^(1/d)>=(r_p+r_q)/2.

Equality between the two ends forces equality at both steps. A proper
inclusion of positive full-dimensional compact convex bodies has
strict volume increase. More explicitly, if x in K_m lies outside
the compact A, it has positive distance from A; mixing x with a fixed
interior ball of K_m with a sufficiently small positive coefficient
gives a positive ball in K_m outside A. Thus the first equality gives
K_m=A exactly.

The standard EQUALITY case of ordinary Brunn--Minkowski for two
positive full-dimensional bodies gives positive homothety when d>=2.
When d=1, every nondegenerate compact interval is already positively
homothetic to every other. Writing K_p=aK+t and K_q=bK+s gives

    K_m=((a+b)/2)K+(t+s)/2,
    g_m=((a+b)/2)g_K+(t+s)/2=(g_p+g_q)/2.

This does not assert general additivity of centroids under Minkowski
addition. The homothety supplied by the equality theorem is the
essential justification. All hypotheses of that standard continuous
theorem hold here. No mixed-integer inequality is invoked.

Every distinct same-parity pair is required. A zero deficit on only
a selected forest would not establish the geometric midpoint closure
used by the finite labeled-point theorem.

## 4. Compactness with fixed P,d,R,v and no mass normalization

The source's compact class has every K_p in the SAME fixed ball R B_d
and volume at least v>0. Bounded compact convex sets are Hausdorff
compact; the finite product remains compact. Volume is continuous
under convex Hausdorff convergence, so the volume lower bounds survive
and every limiting fiber is full-dimensional. Anchored inclusions are
closed: approximate each chosen source point along a convergent
sequence, preserve its fixed convex coefficients, and pass the
resulting target point to the limit. Intersecting these closed
conditions, even over all anchored coefficient vectors, leaves a
compact class X.

For families K^(j)->K, write

    e_j=max_p d_H(K_p^(j),K_p),
    T_j=sum_p vol_d(K_p^(j) symmetric_difference K_p).

Then e_j->0 and T_j->0. The L1 statement follows from pointwise
indicator convergence off the null convex boundaries and the fixed
bounding ball. The total masses obey |M_j-M|<=T_j and are all at
least |P|v; there is no need to impose M=1.

At corresponding points of the same base whose continuous distance
is at most e_j, the raw depths differ by at most

    T_j+|P| kappa_(d-1)R^(d-1)e_j.                    (A)

Indeed a fixed cap's error from the changed fibers is at most T_j.
Normalize a nonvertical continuous normal to unit length; the change
in candidate position changes the cutoff by at most e_j. Every
fiber's corresponding slab has volume at most
kappa_(d-1)R^(d-1)e_j, uniformly over every integer coefficient and
every threshold. For d=1 this uses kappa_0=1. Vertical cap membership
is unchanged because the base is fixed; its error is only T_j.

Within a fixed base fiber the same estimate with T_j=0 proves raw
depth is Lipschitz in its continuous coordinate. A finite union of
compact candidate fibers therefore has an attained maximum. Choosing
Hausdorff-near points in both directions and taking these maxima in
(A) proves convergence of the maximum raw depths. Dividing by the
convergent masses bounded away from zero proves the asserted continuity
of D(K), the maximum normalized depth. This proof stays uniform when
the normalized integer tilt diverges toward a vertical direction.

## 5. The MAXIMUM deficit and the positive compact gap

Because |P|>k, the finite list of distinct same-parity pairs is
nonempty. Every root deficit in formula (3) of the source is
nonnegative by the actual inclusion and BM. Its maximum E(K) is
continuous, and E(K)=0 if and only if ALL listed comparisons are
equalities. This is precisely the input required in Section 3 above.

The sublevel X_bad={D(K)<=Gamma/k} is closed in compact X by the
verified depth continuity, hence compact. If empty, the implication
is vacuous and any positive epsilon works. Otherwise E attains its
minimum e there. Were e=0, the attained family would have all tight
comparisons and hence strict D(K)>Gamma/k, contradicting membership
in X_bad. Therefore e>0. The choice epsilon=e/2 gives exactly

    E(K)<=epsilon implies D(K)>Gamma/k,

and equivalently D(K)<=Gamma/k implies E(K)>epsilon. This confirms
the strict inequality and the boundary E=epsilon in the source, not
just an assertion for E sufficiently near zero without a constant.

The gap depends on the fixed P,d,R,v and may degenerate as any of
those controls changes. In particular the argument gives neither an
explicit dimension-only modulus nor a conclusion when some measured
fiber volumes vanish or intrinsic directions change.

## 6. Scope of the attained-minimum consequence

If |P|=k, a largest fiber has volume at least M/k and its own centroid
already gives raw depth at least Gamma M/k, regardless of the other
fibers. Hence a STRICT below-target family must have |P|>k. Subject
to the separately audited fixed-base positive compact normalization,
the assembly therefore supplies a positive midpoint-root deficit at
some pair of any hypothetical bad minimum.

It does not supply a deformation that reduces depth, or show that
a local minimum must make all midpoint comparisons tight. No boundary
transport energy is identified with the deficit, and overlapping
midpoint contributions are not summed as disjoint mass. The source's
explicit separation of these outstanding steps is correct.

## 7. Added centroid-defect compact gap: PASS

The newly appended Section 5 of the assembly was independently checked.
For two bodies A,B in the common radius-R ball, with volumes at least v,
their centroids satisfy the explicit estimate

    |g_A-g_B| <= (2R/v) vol_d(A symmetric_difference B).

Indeed subtract the two first-moment-over-volume quotients; the first
moment difference is at most R times the symmetric-difference volume,
and the denominator-change term has the same bound after using
|integral_B x dx|<=R|B|. Thus centroid continuity follows uniformly
under the same fixed compact bounds already used for depth continuity.

The maximum centroid-midpoint defect is a maximum of finitely many
continuous nonnegative quantities. If its minimum on a nonempty compact
bad set were zero, ALL midpoint graph identities would hold at the
attained minimizing family. The strict conclusion of Section 1 would
then contradict its bad depth. Hence the centroid-defect minimum is
positive, and taking half of it gives the claimed strict neighborhood.
The empty-bad-set convention remains vacuous and correct.

This uses the sufficient centroid graph condition directly; no BM
equality hypothesis is being added. A positive BM root gap can indeed
occur with a zero centroid defect, so the stronger invariant is not
being identified with the scalar root deficit. A nonzero centroid
defect does force the corresponding root comparison to be strict by
the contrapositive of the correctly proved BM-equality implication.
No deformation or local-minimizer saturation conclusion follows.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
